Hi Laura —

Quick follow-up from our side: we want to make sure the quality monitoring we put in place for AlphaMed has a clear contingency plan for prompt regressions and a deterministic canary trigger/rollback schedule. Our clinical content team is particularly sensitive to hallucinations on the medication-safety prompts.

High-level asks:
- Verify how prompt sets will be versioned and matched to deployed models during canary windows.
- Define alert thresholds for both automatic alerts (regression detected) and human-review triggers.
- Provide an eval-hook integration example we can drop into our CI to gate releases.
- Outline an operational rollback cadence (who approves, expected RTO, whether automatic fallback to a smaller model happens).

We can share sample prompt sets (CSV) and a few example queries if that helps. Could we get a proposed plan and a short canary matrix by EOD Tuesday?

Hi Samantha —

Appreciate the clear asks. I put Marissa and Lauren on copy so we can give you an actionable plan. Below is our suggested approach; Marissa will follow up with the technical snippets and an initial canary matrix attachment.

Summary plan (high level):
1) Prompt sets & versioning:
   - Each approved prompt set is published as a named artifact (promptset-YYYYMMDD-vN). The eval harness will pin to that artifact during canary runs.
   - Runtime associates requests with promptset metadata; canary routing uses that metadata to route a % of traffic to the canary model+promptset pair.

2) Eval harness integration:
   - We'll provide an eval-hook (a Python script + REST call example) that can be incorporated into your CI to run the promptset against the canary model and report metrics (BLEU-ish, custom clinical safety checks).

3) Regression alerts & thresholds:
   - Tiered alerting: P1 (clinical-safety regression) -> immediate paging + pause canary; P2 (quality drop) -> human review + evaluate rollback.
   - Default thresholds we recommend: P1 = any model response that triggers the clinical-safety classifier (threshold 0.85) or a >10% jump in critical-token hallucination rate vs baseline. P2 = 5–10% drop in weighted quality score. These are configurable per account.

4) Canary / rollback policies:
   - Canary windows: 48-hour circuit with evaluations at 2h, 8h, 24h, 48h.
   - Automatic fallback: If a P1 condition is detected at evaluation points, the system pauses canary traffic and routes users to the last-good model variant.
   - Approval flow: Paused canaries require CS + customer sign-off to resume. Rollback where safe is automatic for P1.

Next steps:
- Marissa will attach the canary-trigger matrix + sample eval-hook snippets.
- Samantha: please upload your sample promptset CSV to the Drive link above.
- We'll schedule a 30-minute technical sync Wed 10am PT to walk through the eval-hook.

Laura Bennett

Hey team —

Attached: canary-trigger-matrix-v1.xlsx, eval-hook-snippets.md, promptset-initial.csv (sample). Key items I put into the matrix:

- Canary cohort sizes: 1%, 5%, 20% (gradual ramp).
- Evaluation gates: smoke (latency + 10 sanity queries), safety-run (clinical classifier + blacklist tokens), full-eval (promptset run).
- Decision rules:
  * If smoke fails -> hold and notify (no rollback yet).
  * If safety-run fails -> auto-pause traffic and fallback to last-good.
  * If full-eval shows <5% drop -> continue; 5–10% -> human review; >10% -> auto-rollback.

Eval-hook snippets include:
- A sample GitHub Actions job that triggers the eval harness and posts metrics to your CI dashboard.
- A small Python utility (redwood_eval.py) that:
  * pulls the pinned promptset artifact,
  * queries the canary endpoint for N examples,
  * runs your clinical-safety classifier locally if configured,
  * posts a regression score to your CI.

Operational notes:
- For AlphaMed, I recommend enabling the clinical-safety classifier as a hard gate during canary (we can set the threshold tighter than our default).
- We'll configure two alert channels: PagerDuty for P1 and email/Slack for P2.

Samantha — can you confirm the owners for approvals (who on AlphaMed signs off on canary resume/rollback)? I put down: Samantha Lowe + Dr. Elena Park (Clinical Lead) as placeholders.

-Marissa

Quick operational notes from Product Ops — adding to the plan:

- Canary timing: use local traffic-aware windows (i.e., start canary at low-traffic hours for AlphaMed). Suggested default: 02:00–06:00 PT start for cohort ramps.
- Monitoring retention: store canary evaluation artifacts (inputs + outputs + classifier verdicts) for 90 days to support audits.
- Rollback SLA: automatic fallback is immediate for P1; for P2 we allow up to 4 business hours for human remediation before rollback is triggered automatically.
- Escalation matrix: if Clinical Lead is unreachable, CS can approve temporary pause; but a rollback that affects >10k transactions requires VP approval.

I've also added a small checklist into the Google Doc link: pre-canary runbook, post-eval checklist, and a tidy labeling convention for promptset artifacts.

-Lauren
